stories.title: RK Investors Lands $81M Construction Loan for 299-Unit Charlotte Rental Community
stories.excerpt: An RK Investors-led team obtained an $81 million construction loan for Sutherland at Piper Glen, a 299-unit multifamily development underway in Charlotte’s Piper Glen neighborhood. The financing was provided by Western-Southern Life Insurance Company. The financing was arranged by Nate Sittema, Kristen Reilley and Elliott Voreis with CBRE’s Debt & Structured Finance team. Currently under construction at 9621 Elm Lane, Sutherland at Piper Glen will feature four five-story apartment buildings built atop a single-story parking podium. The community is part of Greenway at Piper Glen, a new master-planned development by RK Investors in South Charlotte. Amenities will include gated access, covered parking, a fitness center, bike storage, coworking spaces, a dedicated golf simulator room, game room, swimming pool, fire pit, grilling areas, pet wash station and coffee bar. Sutherland at Piper Glen is expected to begin leasing in fall 2027, with first units scheduled for delivery in March 2028. The post RK Investors Lands $81M Construction Loan for 299-Unit Charlotte Rental Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RK Investors secured $81M construction loan from Western-Southern Life for 299-unit Charlotte apartment.
Sutherland at Piper Glen in South Charlotte; leasing fall 2027, deliveries March 2028.
Master-planned community with five-story podium buildings; premium amenities signal high-rent positioning.
stories.summary: RK Investors obtained an $81 million construction loan from Western-Southern Life Insurance for Sutherland at Piper Glen, a 299-unit multifamily development in South Charlotte's Piper Glen neighborhood. The four five-story buildings will be built atop a single-story parking podium and feature high-end amenities including coworking, golf simulator, and fitness facilities. Leasing begins fall 2027 with first unit deliveries in March 2028.
stories.impact: Strong financing availability and debt appetite for Charlotte multifamily signals confidence in South Charlotte submarkets as a growth corridor. The developer's emphasis on premium amenities and coworking spaces indicates pricing power and expectation of white-collar demand; a window to monitor absorption rates and rental achievement against this $81M pro forma to benchmark local market strength through 2028.

stories.title: Tech Firms Ink Full-Floor Leases with Moinian Group
stories.excerpt: The Moinian Group has signed approximately 26,000 square feet of new office leases at 245 Fifth Ave. in Manhattan’s Midtown South neighborhood. The two full-floor transactions follow more than 95,000 square feet of leases previously announced at the property. Blacksmith Software: Leased approximately 14,000 square feet. bullets: Tech firms leased 26,000 SF at Moinian Group's 245 Fifth Ave., Manhattan Midtown South.
Full-floor transactions follow 95,000 SF of prior leases; strong office demand recovery signal.
Flexible floor plates and distinctive character driving tenant demand in prime Manhattan location.
stories.summary: The Moinian Group signed approximately 26,000 square feet of new office leases at 245 Fifth Ave. in Manhattan's Midtown South, consisting of two full-floor transactions. This follows more than 95,000 square feet of previously announced leases at the same property, demonstrating sustained demand for high-quality office space with flexible layouts and character in the neighborhood.
stories.impact: Sustained office leasing in prime Manhattan signals a rebound in white-collar employment and workplace demand that typically precedes or accompanies multifamily absorption in close-by residential submarkets. Midtown South's office activity may indicate increased daytime population and residential demand in nearby neighborhoods; however, this is office-centric and should be weighted against the persistent shift to remote/hybrid work before over-indexing on residential upside in Manhattan proper.

stories.title: Pasadena Offices Sell for Residential Conversion
stories.excerpt: NAI Capital Commercial EVPs John S. Archibald and Guillermo Olaiz, alongside senior associate Stephen Lam of the Investment Services Group in the Pasadena office, represented the seller, Star Horizon, LLC, in the sale of ZK Plaza, a 41,586-square-foot office building in Pasadena. The property sold for $13,400,000, representing a 3.5% premium over asking. Located at 600 N. Rosemead Blvd., ZK Plaza occupies a 2.12-acre site in East Pasadena, directly across from General Motors’ advanced design center. Originally built in 1966, the two-story office building was expanded in 1989 and renovated in 2011. Elysian Housing, LLC, plans to redevelop the site into a 133-unit affordable housing community, adaptively reusing the existing office building for 51 units and constructing a new five-story building with 82 units. Archibald said, “This transaction highlights the opportunities for well-located properties in established Southern California markets. ZK Plaza’s location in East Pasadena, near major employers and transportation, offers significant potential for its next chapter.” The post Pasadena Offices Sell for Residential Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Star Horizon sold ZK Plaza (41,586 SF office) in East Pasadena for $13.4M, 3.5% premium.
Elysian Housing converting to 133-unit affordable housing (51 adaptive reuse, 82 new construction).
Located near GM advanced design center and transit; prime adaptive reuse value-add play.
stories.summary: Star Horizon sold ZK Plaza, a 41,586-square-foot office building in East Pasadena, to Elysian Housing for $13.4 million (3.5% above asking). The 1966-built, twice-renovated property will be redeveloped into 133 units of affordable housing, with 51 units in the adapted existing building and 82 new units in a five-story structure on the 2.12-acre site near General Motors' design center.
stories.impact: Office-to-residential conversion in Pasadena signals declining office utility and strong regulatory/financial support for affordable housing in Southern California metros. The adaptive reuse of a 60-year-old office shell suggests construction cost discipline; monitor the feasibility and financing stack (tax credits, gap funding, local incentives) as a template for other CA markets where office obsolescence and housing shortages intersect—and track whether GM's design center presence stabilizes or weakens the submarket's employment base.

stories.title: Lightstone Capital Provides $29.5M Loan for Orange, N.J., Multifamily Development
stories.excerpt: Orange, N.J.-based PEEK Capital, a division of multifamily developer and operator PEEK Properties, has secured a $29.5 million bridge loan on its recently completed multifamily project in Orange known as the Lincoln, Commercial Observer has learned. The bridge loan was provided by Lightstone Group’s real estate debt platform, Lightstone Capital. Daniel Cohen of Ackman-Ziff advised on the transaction. “Peek Properties is a best-in-class sponsor, and Lightstone executed flawlessly on this pre-stabilization bridge loan, which allowed Peek to repatriate equity early in the leasing process,” Cohen told CO in a statement. The loan will support the 102-unit building’s continued lease-up and stabilization, as well as refinance the property’s previous construction financing. Peek previously secured a $20.5 million loan for the development from Amboy Bank in 2024, Real Estate NJ reported. The five-story, full-block apartment building at 407 Highland Avenue in Orange received its final certificate of occupancy in September, according to Lightstone Capital, and has begun leasing a range of one- and two-bedroom residences. “Newly built multifamily properties with proven sponsorship track records have always presented attractive lending opportunities as they transition towards stabilization,” Eugene Rozovsky, senior managing director at Lightstone Capital, said in a statement. The property’s location is one black from N.J. Transit’s Highland Avenue station, offering access to Newark and Midtown Manhattan’s Pennsylvania Station. The cities of Orange and East Orange have been a popular site of luxury apartment development for several years, as renters are priced out of New York City. “The Lincoln continues to attract strong interest from prospective residents, and this refinancing marks an important milestone in the life cycle of the property,” Philip J. The bridge loan will support lease-up, stabilization, and refinancing of the prior $20.5 million construction loan from Amboy Bank (2024).
stories.impact: Bridge financing availability for pre-stabilization multifamily indicates lender confidence in Northern New Jersey as a secondary/tertiary market and appetite for equity recycling. Orange's designation as a lease-up play suggests new supply absorption challenges or slower-than-modeled leasing velocity; monitor the Lincoln's achievement against pro forma and comparable buildings to gauge Orange submarket tightness and whether Northern New Jersey multifamily oversupply is emerging.

stories.title: AJ Capital Partners Lands $52M Refi for Princeton, N.J., Hotel
stories.excerpt: AJ Capital Partners secured a round of financing for one of its hospitality properties in New Jersey, Commercial Observer has learned. GreenOak (formerly BGO) originated a $52 million loan for the 180-room hotel in Princeton, N.J., known as the Graduate by Hilton Princeton, according to sources familiar with the deal. The hotel property at 10 Chambers Street sits directly across from Princeton University. The financing comes with a three-year term and two 12-month extension options, the source said. CBRE’s Tom Rugg, Tom Traynor and Henry Fenmore arranged the financing, but the brokerage declined to comment. GreenOak and AJ Capital did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The hotel, which opened in 2024, is part of AJ Capital’s line of 33 properties known as Graduate Hotels that are near major higher education facilities in both the U.S. and U.K. The Nashville-based real estate firm owns hospitality properties all over the globe, including Wedgewood Village south of Downtown Nashville in the famous music city, as well as Marine & Lawn Golf Hotels, which operates Marine & Lawn Rusacks in St. Andrews, Scotland. The Princeton deal closed on the heels of AJ Capital landing a $62.5 million loan in late August from Peachtree Group to refinance its Graduate by Hilton Nashville hotel property near Vanderbilt University, CO first reported at the time. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: AJ Capital Partners refinanced Graduate by Hilton Princeton (180 rooms) with $52M GreenOak loan.
Hotel opened 2024, located across from Princeton University; 3-year term with 24-month extension options.

stories.summary: AJ Capital Partners secured a $52 million loan from GreenOak (formerly BGO) for the Graduate by Hilton Princeton, a 180-room hotel that opened in 2024 directly across from Princeton University. The financing carries a three-year term with two 12-month extension options. The hotel is part of AJ Capital's portfolio of 33 Graduate-branded properties strategically located near major universities in the U.S. and U.K.
stories.impact: Hospitality financing is tangential to multifamily development; however, the success of the Graduate brand (33 properties at university towns) and refinancing within 2 years of opening signals strong lodging demand near college campuses. This indicates potential upside for multifamily focused on student and young-professional housing in Princeton and similar college towns, especially if the hotel's performance and lender appetite suggests a thriving local economy and visitor economy that supports both overnight and residential demand.

stories.title: Financial Tech Platform Intuit Takes 4K SF at the Orchard in LIC
stories.excerpt: The Orchard, Queens’ tallest residential tower, has signed several new retail leases totaling 7,468 square feet, building owner and developer BLDG Management announced Thursday. In September, financial services platform Intuit, the company behind programs including TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp, signed a 3,546-square-foot lease at the 70-story property at 42-06 Orchard Street in Queens’ Long Island City neighborhood. “The Orchard was designed to be more than a place to live, with residences, amenities and services that give people opportunities to live, work and connect right at home,” Lloyd Goldman, president of BLDG Management, said in a statement. “BLDG has been part of the Long Island City community for more than 60 years, and we wanted the Orchard to build on that legacy by creating a place that serves both residents and the broader neighborhood.” The asking rent and the length of Intuit’s lease were not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space in Long Island City ranges between $18 and $100 per square foot, according to listings on Loopnet.com. Intuit is expected to open its Orchard location in December. In October, Japanese tea and beverage brand Mollytea also signed a new 1,671-square-foot lease at 42-06 Orchard Street, and is expected to open in the second quarter of 2027. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed. In July, Korean beauty supplier Tokimo took 2,251 square feet at the Orchard for what will be its third location in the greater metropolitan area. Tokimo also has locations in Flushing and East Rutherford, N.J. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed. Broker information was not immediately available. Corcoran Sunshine is the exclusive marketing and leasing agent for the Orchard. The building houses 824 residences and is 90 percent leased, according to BLDG. Retail asking rents in LIC range from $18 to $100 per square foot.
stories.impact: Retail leasing by a large tech employer within a residential tower strengthens the live-work model and supports rental demand in LIC. The presence of on-site corporate services (Intuit's office) signals amenity diversification that may drive pricing power and reduce resident churn; this is a positive data point for LIC's maturation as a mixed-use submarket and validates BLDG's positioning. Monitor tenant mix and leasing velocity in LIC residential to see if on-site corporate tenancy becomes a competitive differentiator or marginal amenity.

stories.title: Miami Gardens Leases Public Land for Proposed Hotel
stories.excerpt: The city of Miami Gardens, Fla., this week approved a land lease that sets up the development of a 127-room hotel on city-owned land near Hard Rock Stadium. The proposal calls for a 127-room hotel, the Beckham Hotel Miami Gardens, and a parking garage on part of a 3.5-acre parcel. The hotel – no brand affiliation has been announced yet – and parking garage will be adjacent to a new performing arts center the city plans at the same site. The Beckham in question is not related to soccer star David Beckham. The project is led by Phillip L. Beckham III, a Black developer from Chicago. The city of Miami Gardens, population 116,115, is 59 percent Black, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. “We invest in communities that look like us,” Beckham told the City Council during a meeting this week. The Miami Gardens’ City Council voted unanimously to approve a lease of city-owned vacant property at 18600 Northwest 25th Avenue to P3 Markets and Beckham Hospitality. The deal calls for the developer to pay the city about $18.6 million in rent over the 50-year lease. City documents said the new hotel would be part of a larger project that includes a second hotel and a performing arts center with a 1,200-seat theater. The site is two miles from Hard Rock Stadium, home of the Miami Dolphins, the University of Miami Hurricanes, the annual Orange Bowl, a Formula 1 race and the Miami Open tennis tournament. Billionaire Stephen Ross owns that property and the Dolphins. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Miami Gardens approved 50-year ground lease near Hard Rock Stadium for 127-room hotel + parking.
P3 Markets and Beckham Hospitality to pay city ~$18.6M over lease term; no brand announced.
Hotel and garage adjacent to proposed city performing arts center; minority developer (59% Black city population).
stories.summary: The city of Miami Gardens, Florida, unanimously approved a ground lease on 3.5 acres of city-owned land near Hard Rock Stadium for the Beckham Hotel Miami Gardens, a 127-room hotel with parking garage. Developer Phillip L. Beckham III (Chicago-based Black developer) and P3 Markets will pay the city approximately $18.6 million over the 50-year lease. The project will be adjacent to a planned performing arts center on the same city site.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact; hospitality-focused project. However, the Hard Rock Stadium district's activation with new hotel and performing arts infrastructure may drive upstream population and visitor flows to Miami Gardens, signaling emerging development interest in the submarket. This public-sector ground-lease structure and minority-developer emphasis may indicate policy momentum toward community-oriented development; monitor whether similar catalyst projects emerge in Miami Gardens to inform medium-term residential demand and supply planning for the metro.

stories.title: Hudson Valley Boutique Shop Signs Lease in Manhattan’s Nolita
stories.excerpt: A Beacon, N.Y., knickknack shop is making its New York City debut with a store in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Solstad House General Store signed a five-year, 1,200-square-foot lease at Emmanuel Stark’s 167 Mott Street, with an asking rent of $6,750 per month, according to broker Meridian Retail Leasing. “We reached out to Solstad House directly because we thought the space was a perfect fit for their brand, and they moved fast,” Meridian’s Carson Shahrabani said in a statement. “We went from first email to a signed lease in about two weeks, and they’ll be open for the holidays.” Meridian’s Shahrabani, Noam Aziz and Michael Escava represented both the landlord and tenant in the transaction. “[Solstad House] already has a loyal following in Beacon, and a lot of those customers live in Manhattan,” Aziz said in a statement. “This store gives them a home in the city.” Solstad House primarily sells home goods, food items, puzzles, personal care products and clothing, according to its website. Stark purchased the property between Broome and Grand streets from Platinum Properties for $17 million in 2015. The seven-story building has 26 residential units and two retail units spanning between 500 and 600 square feet on the ground floor, not including cellars, according to CO coverage at the time and property records. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Solstad House General Store (Beacon, N.Y. boutique) signed 5-year, 1,200 SF lease in Manhattan Nolita.
Lease at 167 Mott Street, $6,750/month; Hudson Valley retailer expanding into NYC market.
Beacon customers live in Manhattan; retail brokers positioned as customer follow-the-tenant play.
stories.summary: Solstad House General Store, a boutique shop from Beacon, New York, signed a five-year, 1,200-square-foot lease at 167 Mott Street in Manhattan's Nolita neighborhood at $6,750 per month ($67.50/SF annually). The retailer, which specializes in home goods, food, puzzles, and apparel, is leveraging a loyal Hudson Valley customer base that has relocated to Manhattan. Leasing was completed in approximately two weeks.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the customer migration from Beacon to Manhattan reflects upward mobility and income growth among Hudson Valley residents; if this pattern scales, it signals potential apartment demand growth in Beacon and other Hudson Valley submarkets as bedroom communities for high-earning Manhattan workers, particularly if remote/hybrid work enables commuting. Worth monitoring as a secondary market entry signal.
